reason: The text explicitly portrays the Hebrews (בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל / עַמִּי) as a distinct nation with their own specific land. Most significantly, the passage identifies אֶרֶץ גֹּשֶׁן (the land of Goshen) as the land where the Hebrew people dwell: 'וְהִפְלֵיתִי בַיּוֹם הַהוּא אֶת־ אֶרֶץ גֹּשֶׁן אֲשֶׁר עַמִּי עֹמֵד עָלֶיהָ' (And I will separate in that day the land of Goshen, in which my people stand). The text further distinguishes Hebrew territory by noting that while the rest of Egypt experiences darkness, the Hebrews have light: 'וּלְכָל־ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה אוֹר בְּמוֹשְׁבֹתָֽם' (And for all the children of Israel there was light in their dwellings), establishing them as a nation occupying its own distinct geographical space.
